prompt: A single slender tide gauge staff standing upright in the open sea, seen from slightly above: a tall, narrow, flat wooden board fixed to a thin post that rises straight out of the water. The face of the board is marked from top to bottom with a regular ladder of short plain horizontal tick marks, alternating longer and shorter strokes, the bare scale of a ruler and nothing else on it. The waterline crosses the staff about one third of the way up, with a small ring of ripples drawn as lines around its foot. On top of the staff, a little plain chartreuse yellow-green #b4c424 pennant flag on a thin mast. The staff is small, about one quarter of the image height, and stands in the right half of the image with water all around it. It is drawn in crisp off-white and ink grey line art with fine engraved shading. The left half and the whole bottom of the image are calm open water with only gentle wave lines. Richly detailed engraved nautical chart style, like a fine antique sea chart printed in two inks: the sea built from many layers of fine wave lines and hatching, line density increasing towards the deep water to give depth, tonal bands from deep cerulean at the bottom to lighter cerulean at the top, bathymetric contour lines with small depth soundings drawn as tiny dots, subtle foam strokes and a few glints of light on the crests. Every wave is drawn as visible engraved line work, like a steel engraving, never painted, never smooth. Crisp sharp lines of several weights, intricate but calm, premium print quality, high detail, elegant. No realistic objects, no photographic rendering, no glow, no gradient, no text, no letters, no numbers, no digits, no figures on the staff, no watermark, no horizon, no sky, full-bleed edge to edge, no border, no frame. Palette strictly limited to medium cerulean ocean blue #0072a8 and its tints and shades, off-white #fbfcfd, ink grey #13212b and a touch of chartreuse yellow-green #b4c424 on the pennant only.
